[[Julio de Grazia]] | music = [[Gustavo Beytelman]] | cinematography = [[Adolfo Aristarain]] | editing = | distributor = | released = {{Film date|1976|08|05}} | runtime = 93 minutes | country = Argentina | language = [[Spanish language|Spanish]] | budget = }} '''''No toquen a la nena''''' ("Don't touch the girl") is a 1976 [[Argentina|Argentinian]] film. It is a comedy of manners directed by [[Juan José Jusid]]. The film stars [[Luis Politti]], [[María Vaner]], [[Norma Aleandro]], [[Lautaro Murúa]], [[Pepe Soriano]] and [[Julio de Grazia]], among others. Among the roster of extras, the film featured [[Cecilia Roth]] in her debut performance, 2 years before she would flee Argentina.{{cite web |url=https://es-us.vida-estilo.yahoo.com/cecilia-roth-premio-platino-honor-104122754.html |title=Cecilia Roth, Premio Platino de Honor 2024 |date=March 6, 2024 |website=Yahoo |language=Spanish}} When it was released in Argentina, many of its actors had had to go into exile for reasons of political persecution.{{citation needed |date=June 2024}} The script, written by [[Oscar Viale]] and [[Jorge Goldemberg]],{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ADblg_xP_UgC&dq=%22No+toquen+a+la+nena%22+-wikipedia&pg=PA172 |page=172 |title=Historical Dictionary of the Dirty Wars |first=David |last=Kohut}} received initial approval from the Argentine censors, but was banned before it could be screened. The plot of the film centering on a middle class family dealing with a teen pregnancy, was found to be objectionable by the censors.{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7yGbDwAAQBAJ&dq=%22No+toquen+a+la+nena%22+-wikipedia&pg=PA131 |title=The Argentine Dictatorship and its Legacy |first=Juan |last=Grigero |page=131}} The film has a cast of great Argentinian cinema actors, including [[Julio Chávez]] in a leading role. In the technical team [[Adolfo Aristarain]] acted as assistant director, and [[Juan Carlos Desanzo]] in photography, who would later become prominent directors of Argentinian cinema.{{citation needed |date = June 2024}} ==Plot== Patricia ([[Patricia Calderón]]) is a beautiful 17-year-old teenager who has become pregnant and, in desperation, befriended a friend of her hippie brother, Willy ([[Julio Chávez]]), in whom she finds support and understanding. When her father ([[Luis Politti]]), an Argentine classic of Italian descent, found out, first she hit Willy hard, believing her to be the father, and then she sought to marry her to her daughter to "save face" ==Cast== * [[Luis Politti]] as Augusto{{cite web |url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/peliculas-series/peliculas/no-toquen-a-la-nena-572834/actores |title=Reparto de No toquen a la nena |website= La Vanguardia}} * [[María Vaner]] as Haydée * [[Norma Aleandro]] as Andrea * [[Lautaro Murúa]] as Horacio * [[Pepe Soriano]] as Severino Di Filippi "El Nono" * [[Julio De Grazia]] as Bambi * [[Pierina Dealessi]] as La Mamma * [[Gustavo Rey]] debuted as Javier{{cite web |url=https://es-us.vida-estilo.yahoo.com/gustavo-rey-galancito-conoci%C3%B3-%C3%A9xito-152802550.html |title=Gustavo Rey: fue "galancito", conoció el éxito abrumador, pero debió alejarse del medio por un tema personal |date=November 14, 2023 |first=Lilian |last=Podesta |website=La Nacion}} * [[Julio Chávez]] as Willy * [[Cecilia Roth]] debuted as Cecilia * [[Patricia Calderón]] as Patricia * [[Alberto Busaid]] as Nacho * [[Lidia Catalano]] as Dorita * [[Claudio Lucero]] as Capataz * [[Patricio Contreras]] as Peón * [[Juan Manuel Tenuta]] as Funes * [[Aldo Marinelli]] as El Médico * [[Chunchuna Villafañe]] as La Mercedes * [[Nora Renzi]] as Flequillo * [[Oscar Viale]] as Porta * [[Atilio Polverini]] * [[Divina Gloria]] * [[Gonzalo Urtizberea]] ==External links== * {{IMDb title|id =|title =No toquen a la nena }} ==References== {{reflist}} {{DEFAULTSORT:No Toquen A La Nena}} [[Category:1976 films]] [[Category:Argentine comedy films]] [[Category:1970s Spanish-language films]] [[Category:1976 comedy films]] [[Category:Spanish-language comedy films]] [[Category:Films directed by Juan José Jusid]] [[Category:1970s Argentine films]]
